The '''2014 Virtual Card Pool Reset''' was the [[Players Committee]] decision to cut the SWCCG virtual card pool to a small base set rather than clean it up with errata. The Advocate Council announced it as '''Reset of Standard Format''' on 25 July 2014.<ref name="reset-announce">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/reset-of-standard-format/ Reset of Standard Format], Advocate Council (byline darkjediknight11), Players Committee (25 July 2014). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20170306155342/http://www.starwarsccg.org/reset-of-standard-format/ Internet Archive, 6 March 2017]</ref> The first post-reset legal lists, [[Virtual Set 0]] and a Virtual Set 1 Preview, were posted as PDFs on 25 September 2014.<ref name="reset-pdf">[http://web.archive.org/web/20141009180356id_/http://www.starwarsccg.org/wp/pdf-of-reset-list-posted-virtual-set-0-and-virtual-set-1-preview/ PDF of Reset List Posted &mdash; Virtual Set 0 and Virtual Set 1 Preview] (Wayback id_ capture), byline September 25th, 2014</ref>

== Why reset ==

The Advocates weighed a '''cleanup''' (surgical errata or scrapping problem cards) against a '''complete reset''' that trimmed virtual cards to a small base set. They chose the reset unanimously.<ref name="reset-announce" /> Their reasons included one PDF of legal virtual text instead of mass errata to remember, past problems with mass-errata changes, and design opportunities for volunteers in a smaller pool.<ref name="reset-announce" /> They also cited casual players' time budgets and wanted a more complete fix than a &ldquo;band-aid&rdquo;.<ref name="reset-announce" />

== Base set and text rule ==

The base set was planned at roughly 75 cards per side.<ref name="reset-announce" /><ref name="c1g">[https://blog.categoryonegames.com/resetting-star-wars-ccg/ Resetting Star Wars CCG], Category One Games</ref> Virtual cards that can go in a '''reserve deck''' kept their game text: &ldquo;If you know a card now, you will know the card post-Reset&rdquo;.<ref name="reset-announce" /> The announcement planned a preliminary base list by 1 August 2014 and beta play at Worlds in Toronto and the European Championship.<ref name="reset-announce" />

[[Virtual Set 0]] (Base Set) cards were unchanged from their pre-reset versions except for some Defensive Shields; Virtual Set 1 Preview cards had various minor tweaks.<ref name="reset-pdf" />

== Formats: Standard and Legacy ==

* New '''Standard''': post-reset virtual cards. A new graphical V-set icon was planned, and existing slips stayed usable for cards that remained legal.<ref name="reset-announce" />
* New '''Legacy''': all pre-reset virtual cards, in a Master Legacy PDF. The pool stays fixed unless D&amp;D later supports Legacy balance.<ref name="reset-announce" /><ref name="reset-pdf" />
* The VS0 and VS1 Preview PDFs were '''legal immediately''' for Standard sanctioned play.<ref name="reset-pdf" />

== What was not changed ==

* The Advocates had no plans to change Decipher cards or Decipher rules.<ref name="reset-announce" />
* There was no set rotation after the Reset, following a player survey.<ref name="reset-announce" />

== Packaging: blocks &rarr; V0 then V1 ==

The Advocates planned to drop blocks for single sets: base set '''V0''', then a new numbering starting at '''V1'''.<ref name="reset-announce" /> These are [[Virtual Set 0]] and [[Virtual Set 1]].

== Virtual Block 9.2 ==

The announcement said V-set '''9.2''' would not be released in its current form. A mini set of about 12 cards for Worlds would replace it, and the intern work would be remolded later.<ref name="reset-announce" /> VB '''9.1''' (''Republic at War'') had shipped on 10 January 2014. See [[Cancelled Virtual Sets#V-set / Virtual Block 9.2|Cancelled Virtual Sets]].
